subject: Acadia: feature escrow & sprint allocation for EHR mapping
messages:
From: Liam Foster <liam.foster@acadiahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acadia: request for feature escrow & sprint allocation for EHR mapping

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Acadia is excited about the lower-latency routing and the model-control guarantees you showed. We are ramping integration work with our vendor (MedMap) and have one hard requirement from procurement and our security team: we need a committed delivery window for the EHR field-mapping feature (ability to pin/escape model behavior for specific tenant mappings) and a short-term "feature escrow" agreement that assures us a compatible model variant will be available during our go-live window.

High level ask: can Redwood commit a sprint allocation (2 dev weeks) in June to implement the mapping API and a formal escrow/rollback mechanism so we can finish validation with PHI synthetic data? Procurement needs this tied to the SOW and an implementation timeline to approve the order.

I attached a draft SOW and our preliminary mutual action plan for visibility (we'll share the final vendor mapping spec this week).

Can you confirm feasibility and a rough ETA by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Liam Foster
Director of Integrations
Acadia Health
Attachments: SOW-Acadia-v2.pdf (stub), mapping-spec-placeholder.xlsx (to follow)

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Fwd: Acadia: request for feature escrow & sprint allocation for EHR mapping

On Mon, May 7, 2028 at 10:04 AM karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com> wrote:
> Folks — forwarding the request from Acadia (deal DEAL-8742). Key points: 2-week sprint allocation in June to build a tenant-specific EHR field-mapping endpoint + an escrow/rollback plan that ensures we can pin a model variant or revert changes if mapping validation fails.

Thanks for the context. Short answer: likely feasible but depends on scope. Technical notes and constraints:

- Mapping endpoint: we can expose a per-tenant mapping config that lives in our config-service and feeds into the pre-tokenization step. Estimated deliverable: ~6 dev days (backend + API + unit tests) + 2 days QA/validation. We should allocate 2 full dev weeks to account for integration with MedMap test harness.
- Escrow/pinning: we already support model variant pinning for customers on Dedicated tiers; for Hosted we can implement a temporary variant pin with a config flag. That work is ~3 dev days (coord with runtime + routing).
- Rollback automation: add a toggle to revert mapping configs and promote a fallback model variant — 2 dev days.
- Non-dev tasks: docs, runbook, and release notes (1–2 days).

Total engineer effort estimate: 13–15 dev days (fits in a 2-week allocation with 2 engineers). Risks: integration test data containing PHI must be synthetic; we'll need a pairing session with Acadia's integration engineer to validate mapping rules.

Next steps I need from sales/CS: confirm acceptance of a scope cut if we need to hit a hard date (e.g., reduce to API + pinning, leave rollback for post-go-live). Also share the MedMap test harness before end of week so we can run a dry integration. I'll open SERV-1429 and link it here.

Ben
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Related ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SERV-1429
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 May 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acadia: request for feature escrow & sprint allocation for EHR mapping

Thanks Ben — that estimate looks reasonable. From a commercial perspective: Acadia is a mid-size health system and this is a seeded pilot expected to roll into a larger multi-region contract if successful. We can offer a limited prioritization in exchange for:

- Signed SOW with a delivery milestone in June (we need the SOW updated to include the sprint dates and acceptance criteria)
- A one-time implementation credit of 10% on the first-year usage commit (to offset the prioritization cost)
- Commitment to a 12-month Dedicated tier evaluation post-pilot (we can make this contingent, but it strengthens ROI).

If Sales confirms the SOW update and the customer accepts the credit, Marissa / CS will approve the sprint slot. I recommend we split the work: Sprint week 1 for API + pinning (blocking deliverable), Sprint week 2 for rollback automation and integration tests. That reduces risk for the June milestone.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Liam Foster <liam.foster@acadiahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 May 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acadia: request for feature escrow & sprint allocation for EHR mapping

Karthik / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed commercial arrangement. Acadia accepts the 10% implementation credit and will update the SOW to include the June sprint milestone and the acceptance criteria you outlined (API + pinning in week 1, rollback automation + integration QA in week 2). Procurement will attach a short addendum to the SOW referencing the escrow expectation.

Two asks from our side before you lock the sprint:
- Can you confirm the dates for the two-week slot (we prefer Jun 10–21 but can be flexible).
- Please add a short runbook item that lists rollback steps and the contact for emergency rollback during the first week after go-live.

Once we have those two items in the SOW addendum we'll route for signature. Appreciate the team moving on this — excited to get the pilot started.

Best,
Liam Foster
Director of Integrations
Acadia Health
